errors.wrong: The lesson gives the FIBA no-charge semicircle as "1.25 metre" with no edge named. FIBA Official Basketball Rules 2026, 2.5.7: "A semi-circle line with the radius of 1.30 m measured from the point on the court beneath the exact centre of the basket to the outer edge of the semi-circle." All lines are 5 cm wide (2.4), so the inner edge is at 1.25 m (Wikipedia: "The FIBA adopted the NBA's restricted area arc with a marginally wider radius of 1.25 meters"). NBA Rule 1: "A Restricted Area shall be marked with a half-circle 4' from the center of the basket ring". NBA Rule 10 Section VII is the Defensive Three-Second Rule.
errors.correct: Say exactly: 1.25 m to the inner edge and 1.30 m to the outer edge of the 5 cm line; do not bundle unsourced NBA claims into the description.

diff.after: [Rules] FIBA Versus NBA: Semicircle, Backboard and Defensive Three Seconds | Compare FIBA's no-charge semicircle, 1.25 m to the inner edge and 1.30 m to the outer edge of its 5 cm line, with NBA rules.

errors.wrong: Judge-chosen line (29 words, over the 25-word limit): "[Practice] Judge Shooting by the Next-Day Cold Set | After the general warm-up, log your first ten elbow jump shots before taking any other elbow shots, because same-shot repetition can make today's percentage look better than next-day retention." Evidence: blocked (same-shot) practice scores best during practice, while varied practice retains and transfers better (Shamshiri et al. 2025); the app judges a skill by the first ten shots the next day (the cold set).
errors.correct: The same claim in at most 25 words, without saying blocked practice always inflates a score.

diff.after: [Practice] Judge Shooting by the Next-Day Cold Set | Next day, after warming up, log your first ten elbow jump shots, because same-shot practice can make today's percentage look better than retention.

errors.wrong: Judge-chosen line (29 words, over the 25-word limit): "[Practice] Shuffle Scales After One Correct Run | Play G, D, F and A major scales correctly once each, then shuffle their order, because random-order practice is retained better two days later even though it feels harder." Evidence: random-order practice of short melodies was retained better at two days than fixed-order practice while learners judged the opposite (Abushanab and Bishara 2013); the benefit holds for short units once learned (Verwey et al. 2021).
errors.correct: The same claim in at most 25 words.
